title: Interface Default Methods
concept: Default methods in interfaces provide shared implementations that all implementors inherit — reducing boilerplate across types.
why: Without defaults, every implementor must write identical boilerplate methods. Default methods let you write it once and share with all implementations.
tips: Default methods reduce boilerplate — implementors provide minimum, get maximum
Default methods can call required methods — build rich behavior from simple building blocks
Override defaults when the default behavior doesn't fit your type
Keep defaults simple — complex defaults are hard to reason about when overridden
common_mistakes: Writing defaults that don't make sense for all implementors — defaults should be truly universal
Default methods that are too complex — they should be thin wrappers around required methods
Forgetting that default methods CAN be overridden — don't rely on default behavior in critical paths
